P1.evidence: The call opened with four minutes of complaint about the booking process, and the frame arrived as a defence rather than a structure: 'Really, my job is to make sure that, number one, we can definitely help, that you would have a high likelihood of being successful, that this is a fit for what you're looking for. And if all those stars align, then obviously we can talk about what it looks like to work with Trevor.' Two of the four parts, and no frame-agreement question was ever asked. Open question did run — 'Well, yeah, man. I mean, how can we potentially help?' P1a is N/A: no setter suffix and no setter notes existed, the booking ran through an automated text flow. Handling of the opening grievance was genuinely good and defused it, but it is not the scripted phase.

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in the batch on the things that were asked and the weakest on the things that were not. Health conditions asked properly — 'So you have like a health scare or something like what made you realize that?' produced sleep apnoea, low testosterone, blood pressure, a severe fatty liver with scarring, and a family history. Injury history asked in real depth: 'what sort of things have you done to try to rehab the shoulders and maybe physio?' and 'what actually originally damaged them?' produced the full acromion and four-surgery history. Current training asked directly and honestly answered — 'Right now, I haven't been doing anything.' Diet asked — 'what's normal eating for you look like right now?' But age, height and weight were all volunteered and never asked; occupation was volunteered early and only explored an hour later as post-price rapport; and sleep and energy were never asked despite the prospect disclosing sleep apnoea unprompted, which is exactly the condition P2h exists to catch.

P3.evidence: Good on what and why-now, absent on who-else. 'what are some of the activities that you're looking to maybe get muscle for? Is it to keep doing martial arts or is it more just to kind of maintain your physique?' did the surface work, and 'Was there any particular reason why you reached out, you know, now?' is the question that unlocked the whole call — the weight-loss threshold, the energy return, and then the heart-attack line. What never ran: the wife appears throughout ('I take my girl out to dinner', the condo, the mortgage) and was never once made part of the stake; 'who else does that impact' would have been the strongest lever available and was never asked. The reflect-back at 00:39:14 was interpretive rather than confirmatory and risky in its wording — telling a former Marine 'we can get into like a, almost like a victim state' without a check question. The prospect agreed anyway, but by luck rather than technique.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were explored only through the rehab lens — 'what sort of things have you done to try to fix that?' — never as a fitness history. The prospect handed over the root cause unprompted and in perfect form: 'I have spent years looking for a trainer. And everybody that I find, they don't have answers' and 'it's all the same, everybody's bench and curl... just the same stuff from different people.' The rep summarised it back ('you either get surgery again, maybe, or don't work out, or find a way to somebody out there who can show you things that you can still do') but never asked for it, so under the scoring rule it does not count. P90X, the trainer who put him on the peptide, and three unused kettlebells sitting in his basement for three years were all mentioned and none were followed with 'what happened with that'.

P5.evidence: Never ran, on the call in this batch where it would have mattered most. The prospect supplied the entire consequence frame himself — 'if you don't do something, you're going to have a heart attack and you're going to die. It's pretty simple' and 'I was told last year, I have a fatty liver... they said you have a severe fatty liver with a tiny bit of scarring' — and the rep asked only a backward-looking question about what triggered the realisation. No 'what does the next two years look like if nothing changes', no 'are you willing to settle for that', no line in the sand. The only forward-cost statement came 45 minutes later and was a throwaway: 'I also don't think it's the best for you to go another few months without getting something going.' A man who believes inaction kills him was allowed to leave planning to wait several more months.

P6.evidence: No commitment check at any point. Price was given on request at 01:01:17 with nothing banked behind it. The prospect volunteered the yes the phase is designed to extract — 'nobody needs to sell me on what you guys are doing like I already get it' and later 'I knew I wanted to do this before I even talked to you today. I've been wanting to do this for like two months' — and it was never converted into a commitment the rep could hold him to when the money objection arrived. Neither P6a nor P6b was asked in any form.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — checkout and financing links were shared live in the Zoom chat and worked through together — so the phase applies, and payment was not collected. The rep never actually asked for the sale on a 102-minute call with a prospect who said he had already decided. The exchange that should have been the close instead became logistics: 'what do I do when I'm ready to do this? How do I reach out to you again?' answered with 'you're like in our system now.' Steps 2 to 4 were unreachable without payment.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest money objection in the batch and the play ran about half. Ran: some of the financial picture (annual income $65-70k, flat commission with no base, mortgage, car payment, two months without a sale, self-reported good credit), a credit-card suggestion, and live financing walked through on screen. Did not run: the isolation question first — 'finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%' was never asked, which matters because the medical fit question was still genuinely open; no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place'; no explicit permission-to-ask framing; and none of cash on hand, number of cards, available credit per card, used versus available, or investments. Most of what the rep learned about the finances came because this prospect volunteers everything, not because the play was run. The rep then abandoned it outright: 'Obviously, money's money. If you don't have that much to invest, it is what it is.'

Explicit not-now-later objection — 'over the next few months, save, you know, half of that' and 'I just got to save a little money.' None of the play ran. No 'things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The rep had the strongest possible version of that argument available and unused: a prospect who had just said inaction would give him a heart attack, and whose income is lumpy enough that 'a couple of good months' may never arrive. The one attempt was a single soft line.

Clinical fit objection, the known gap in the script and the most consequential instance of it in the corpus so far. The prospect raised it himself as the central question of the call — 'I don't know if he can help me... is there an alternative or something that would still allow me to do his program' and 'if Trevor said, you know what, John, I don't think this is a good fit for you.' With no scripted path, the rep improvised reassurance ('a lot of our clients come to us with shoulder injuries... a lot of them are able to rehab those, just through what we teach them'), a no-excuses frame, and an unconditional refund promise. Nothing in the script tells a rep to ask whether a clinician has cleared loaded ballistic work, and nothing in this call did.

Free-substitute objection, the second known script gap. 'I guarantee that if I do 90% of everything that he has by watching videos, it's probably going to do what I want to do anyway.' The rep conceded it — 'Yeah, it's definitely better than sitting on the couch' — which is the opposite of the required move. Nobody argued that free videos cannot tell a man with bilateral cuff tears which movements will re-tear them, which is both the truthful differentiator and the safety argument, and the rep had it sitting right there.
No think-about-it stall — the prospect gave a specific savings plan rather than a vague deferral.
Married and referenced his wife repeatedly but never made the decision contingent on her.
No fear or doubt about the programme working; if anything his belief was excessive.

notes: Excellent rapport and real depth on the medical history, and then no process at all after discovery — no consequence frame, no commitment check, no ask for the sale in 102 minutes on a prospect who had already decided and said so. The rep conceded the free-video substitute and conceded the money, and the call ended with the prospect owning every next step. But the coaching priority here is not conversion: this prospect has irreparable bilateral rotator cuff damage, is avoiding his surgeon, and was told 'we'll find a way around whatever the issue is'. The process fix and the safety fix are the same one — add a clinical clearance gate to P2 and stop the call there when it fails.
